Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:1.english: And due to causing the poor to be idle - For they would not know when he would harvest them.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:2.hebrew: מפני החשד - שהעוברין רואין בגמר קצירו שהוא מכלה את הכל, לא ידעו שנתנה כבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:2.english: Due to suspicion - For passersby, seeing at the conclusion of his harvest that he is finishing off everything, will not know that he already gave it.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:3.english: And because of “You shall not wholly reap” - For it implies the time of completion [of the harvest].

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:4.hebrew: אטו כולהו - הני דאמרן, לא טעמא דלא תכלה קא מפרשי — מאי שנא שעת כילוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:4.english: Are all of them - These [reasons] that we stated, do they not explain the rationale of "You shall not finish" — why the time of completion is different?

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:5.hebrew: אמר רבא מפני הרמאין - העוברין על לא תכלה, ואומרים: כבר הנחנוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:1:5.english: Rava said: Due to the cheaters - [Those] who transgress [the prohibition of] "You shall not wholly reap," and say: "We have already left it."

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:2:1.hebrew: שתי פיות - שהנרות שלהם של חרס הן ומכוסין, ועושים לו נקב בצדי כסויו להכניס לו הפתילה, והוא הפה. ולמעלה בכיסויו יש נקב קטן, וגם חלל יש למעלה מן הכסוי, וממלאו שמן והוא נכנס דרך הנקב מעט מעט. אם יש בו שני נקבים משני צדדין, עולה לשני בני אדם — למהדרין העושין נר לכל אחד ואחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:2:1.english: Two spouts - For their lamps were of earthenware and covered, and they make a hole in it at the side of its cover to insert the wick into it, and that is the "mouth" [i.e., spout]. And above, on its cover, there is a small hole, and there is also a hollow [depression] above the cover; and one fills it with oil, and it enters through the hole little by little. If it has two holes on two sides, it counts for two people — for the mehadrin, who make a lamp for each and every person.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:2:2.hebrew: עשאה כמדורה - שהאש מתחברת לאמצעיתה, ואינו דומה לנר:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:2:2.english: He made it like a bonfire - For the fire joins together in its center, and it does not resemble a lamp.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:3:1.hebrew: נר ביתו ונר חנוכה - נר ביתו בשבת, והוא עני ואין לו כדי לקנות שמן לשתי נרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:3:1.english: The lamp for his home and the Hanukkah lamp - [This refers to] the lamp for his home on Shabbat, and he is poor and does not have enough [money] to buy oil for two lamps.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:3:2.hebrew: שלום ביתו - והכי אמרינן לקמן (שבת דף כה:): ותזנח משלום נפשי — זו הדלקת נר בשבת, שבני ביתו מצטערין לישב בחשך:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:3:2.english: Peace in his home - And so we say later on (Shabbat 25b): "And my soul is removed far off from peace" — this is kindling the Shabbat lamp, for the members of his household are distressed to sit in darkness.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:1.hebrew: בנים תלמידי חכמים - דכתיב (משלי ו׳:כ״ג): "כי נר מצוה ותורה אור" — על ידי נר מצוה דשבת וחנוכה בא אור דתורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:1.english: Sons who are Torah scholars - As it is written (Proverbs 6:23): "For a mitzvah is a lamp, and Torah is light" — through the mitzvah lamp of Shabbat and Hanukkah, the light of Torah comes.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:2.english: Of Rabbi Avin the carpenter - A craftsman of wood.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:4.hebrew: חליף ותני - עובר ושונה, כלומר: עובר תמיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:4.english: Passing by and repeating - Passing by and repeating, that is to say, passing by constantly.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:5.hebrew: דבי נשא - אביו, ואיכא דאמרי: חמיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:5.english: Of the family home - His father; and some say: his father-in-law.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:4:6.english: [He] emerged from them - For one's son-in-law is like his son.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:1.english: Would delay and kindle - [She would kindle] the Shabbat lamp close to nightfall.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:2.hebrew: לא ימיש - קרא יתירא הוא להך דרשה, דהא כתיב: וה' הולך לפניהם יומם:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:2.english: Departed not - It is a superfluous verse for this exposition, for behold, it is [already] written: "And the Lord went before them by day..."

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:3.hebrew: עמוד הענן - של יום משלים אורו לעמוד האש, שהיה עמוד האש בא קודם שישקע עמוד הענן. אלמא, אורח ארעא בהכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:3.english: The pillar of cloud - [The pillar] of the day would extend its light to the pillar of fire, for the pillar of fire would arrive before the pillar of cloud set. Consequently, this is proper conduct.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:4.english: To advance [the lighting] - While it is still broad daylight.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:5:6.english: That one does not light early - For it is not recognizable that it is for Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:6:2.english: He will have sons who are Sages - And his love for them is like [that of] a father for a son.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:6:3.english: And if he is not capable of this - That he is not accustomed to engage in Torah study.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:7:1.english: And it is designated for burning - For it is forbidden to be eaten.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:7:2.english: That it is a mitzva upon him to burn it - Lest one come through it to a mishap of eating [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:7:3.english: Lest he tilt [it] - So that it will burn quickly.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:7:4.hebrew: ביום טוב - דליכא למיחש להטייה, לישתרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:7:4.english: On a Festival - Since there is no concern of tilting [the lamp], it should be permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 23b:8:2.hebrew: בערב שבת - והוא צריך להדליקה מבעוד יום, נמצא שורף קדשים ביו"ט. ולקמן בפרקין (שבת דף כד:) ילפינן מקראי דאין שורפין:
Rashi on Shabbat 23b:8:2.english: On Shabbat eve - And he must light it while it is still day, so it turns out that he is burning consecrated items on the Festival. And later in our chapter (Shabbat 24b), we derive from verses that one may not burn [them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:3:1.hebrew: הדר פשטה נר חנוכה עדיף משום פרסומי ניסא - ונראה לרשב"א, כשחל ר"ח טבת להיות בשבת, שיש להפטיר בנרות דזכריה משום פרסומי ניסא, ולא בהשמים כסאי, שהיא הפטרת ר"ח. ועוד, כיון שהמפטיר קורא בשל חנוכה, יש לו להפטיר מענין שקרא. ומה שמקדימים לקרות בשל ר"ח — משום דבקריאת התורה, כיון דמצי למיעבד תרוייהו, תדיר ופרסומי ניסא, עבדינן תרוייהו ותדיר קודם; אבל היכא דלא אפשר למעבד תרוייהו, פרסומי ניסא עדיף. ועוד, דבקריאת התורה אין כל כך פרסומי ניסא, שאינו מזכיר בה נרות כמו בהפטרה. ועוד נראה לרשב"א, דעל כן הקדימו של ר"ח, כדי שהמפטיר יקרא בשל חנוכה ויפטיר בנרות דזכריה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:3:1.english: "He then resolved it: The Hanukkah lamp takes precedence due to publicity of the miracle" - And it appears to the Rashba that when Rosh Chodesh Tevet falls on Shabbat, one should read the haftarah of the lamps of Zechariah (Zechariah 2:14–4:7) due to publicity of the miracle, and not "The heaven is My throne" (Isaiah 66:1), which is the haftarah for Rosh Chodesh. And furthermore, since the maftir reads from [the portion] of Hanukkah, he should read the haftarah on the subject of that which he read. And as for the fact that they read [the portion] of Rosh Chodesh first — [that is] because in the Torah reading, since it is possible to fulfill both — [that which is] frequent and [that which involves] publicity of the miracle — we fulfill both, and the frequent [practice] takes precedence; but where it is not possible to fulfill both, publicity of the miracle takes precedence. And furthermore, in the Torah reading there is not as much publicity of the miracle, as lamps are not mentioned in it as [they are] in the haftarah. And furthermore, it appears to the Rashba that for this reason they placed [the reading] of Rosh Chodesh first: so that the maftir would read from [the portion] of Hanukkah and [consequently] read the haftarah of the lamps of Zechariah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג חזא דהוו רגילי בשרגא - פי': הבעל והאשה; לכך אמר: "תרי גברי רברבי נפקי מהכא". ולקמן אמר: "חזא דהוה רגילה" — האשה לבדה; לכך קאמר דנפיק חד גברא רבא בזכותה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:4:1.english: This is the reading: "He saw that they were accustomed to the lamp" - Meaning, [both] the husband and the wife; therefore [Rav Huna] said: "Two great men will emerge from here." And later on [the Gemara] states: "He saw that she was accustomed" — [referring to] the woman alone; therefore it states that one great man emerged in her merit.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:4:2.hebrew: דבי נשא דרב שיזבי - אומר ר"ת, דכבר נפטר אביו, לכך קאמר בהאי לישנא; דאי מחיים — הוה ליה למימר "דבי אבוה". ואומר ר"ת בשם רבינו שמואל, שכשכותבין כתובה: אם אבי הכלה מחיים — כותבין "דהנעלת ליה מבי אבוה", ואם כבר מת — כותבין "דהנעלת ליה מבי נשא". ולרשב"א נרא', דאפי' מחיים אשכחן דקאמר "בי נשא", בפרק מי שהחשיך (לקמן שבת דף קכו.): לוי בריה דרב הונא בר חייא אשכחיה לגבלא דבי נשא דקגביל וספי לתוריה, בטש ביה, אתא אבוה אשכחיה, כו'. ויכול לכתוב בכתובה כאשר ירצה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:4:2.english: "Of the family home of Rav Sheizvi" - Rabbeinu Tam says that his father had already passed away; that is why [the Gemara] uses this phrasing, for if [his father were still] alive, it should have said "of his father's house" [devei avuha]. And Rabbeinu Tam says in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel that when writing a ketubah, if the bride's father is alive, they write: "that she brought in to him from her father's house" [de-han'alat leih mi-bei avuha]; and if he has already died, they write: "that she brought in to him from her family's house" [de-han'alat leih mi-bei nasha]. And to the Rashba it appears that even during [the father's] lifetime, we find that [the Gemara] says "bei nasha", in the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shehecheshikh" (below, Shabbat 126a): "Levi the son of Rav Huna bar Chiyya found the kneader of the family home [devei nasha] kneading and feeding [it] to the oxen; he kicked him. His father came and found him, etc." And [therefore,] one may write in the ketubah whichever [phrasing] he wishes.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:7:1.hebrew: גזרה יו"ט אטו שבת - וא"ת: בכל שמנים שאין מדליקין בהן בשבת נגזור יו"ט אטו שבת! ובמתני' תנן: "אין מדליקין בשמן שריפה ביו"ט", משמע דבשאר שמנים מדליקין! וי"ל: דבשאר שמנים, דכיון דאין נמשכין אחר הפתילה, כי שרי ביו"ט לא אתי למישרי בשבת, דפשיטא הוא דאיכא למיגזר בהן שמא יטה. אבל שמן שריפה, אי שרי ביו"ט, איכא למטעי ואתי למשרי בשבת, כיון דנמשך אחר הפתילה, לפי שאינו פשוט לעולם דטעמא דמתוך שמצוה עליו לשורפו גזרה שמא יטה. הקשה ה"ר אליעזר: דהכא מפרש רבה דטעמא גזרה יו"ט אטו שבת, ולקמן (שבת דף כד:) מפיק מקרא ד"הוא לבדו"! והשיב לו רבינו שמואל: דע"כ לקמן הוי רבא שהוא אחר אביי, והכא רבה, שהרי משיב לו אביי תלמידו, וגם פליג עליה רב חסדא חבירו. אך קשה: מאי פריך הכא אביי: "אלא מעתה ביו"ט לישתרי", והוא גופיה מפיק לקמן דאין מדליקין בשמן שריפה מ"עולת שבת בשבתו"?! ונראה לפרש: דאביי ורבא לקמן לא קיימי אמאי דקאמר: מ"ט אין מדליקין, לפי שאין שורפין קדשים ביו"ט, ולית להו האי גזרה [תרומה אטו קדשים]; אלא קיימי לפרושי מנ"ל שאין שורפין קדשים ביום טוב. ורשב"א מפרש הכי: "אלא מעתה ביום טוב לישתרי" — אי אמרת בשלמא דמיירי ביום טוב שחל בערב שבת, וטעמא לפי שאין שורפין קדשים ביום טוב, כדמוקי לה רב חסדא — שפיר; אלא כיון שאמרת טעמא דאין מדליקין בשבת גזירה שמא יטה, השתא לא מצי לפרושי דביום טוב אין מדליקין לפי שאין שורפין קדשים ביו"ט, דהא מה שייך יו"ט למיתני הכא, כיון דביו"ט טעמא אחרינא הוא? אלא צריך לפרש דביו"ט נמי שמא יטה, ומאי יטה שייך ביו"ט? ולפ"ז מתיישב לישנא "אלא מעתה", דמשמע שיש לפרש בענין אחר שלא יקשה "ביו"ט לישתרי", ולא קשה דאביי אדאביי. ואם תאמר: דהכא גזר רבה יו"ט אטו שבת, ושבת גופיה שמא יטה, א"כ סבר דגזרינן גזרה לגזרה! ובריש פירקין קאמר: "היא גופה גזרה, ואנן ניקום ונגזור גזרה לגזרה?!", ולא גזרי' נתן לתוך חלב מהותך שמן אטו לא נתן, דבלא נתן נמי לא אסור אלא אטו שאין מהותך, אע"ג דבחלב מהותך גזרינן גזרה לגזרה, דגזרי' אטו שאינו מהותך, ושאינו מהותך אטו שמא יטה — הא לא חשיב גזרה לגזרה, דכשאינו מהותך ודאי יטה, לפי שאינו נמשך אחר הפתילה; אבל הכא, משום שמצוה עליו, לית לן למימר ודאי יטה! ותירץ ר"י: דהכא לא חשיב גזירה לגזרה, דיו"ט ושבת כי הדדי נינהו, כדאמרינן בפרק במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף ס. ושם) גבי סנדל המסומר. וקשה לרשב"א: דהכא גזרינן יו"ט אטו שבת, ובריש כל הכלים (לקמן שבת דף קכד. ושם) מסקינן דלא גזרינן! ושמא אין להשוות גזרות של חכמים זו לזו, אותם שאינם במלאכה אחת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:7:1.english: A decree [regarding] a Festival on account of Shabbat - And if you say: For all oils with which one may not light on Shabbat, let us decree [a prohibition on] a Festival on account of Shabbat! And in the Mishnah (below, 24b) we learned: "One may not light with burnt oil on a Festival," which implies that with other oils one may light! And it can be answered: With other oils, since they are not drawn after the wick, even if it is permitted on a Festival, one will not come to permit [them] on Shabbat, for it is obvious that there is reason to decree regarding them lest one tilt [the lamp]. However, with burnt oil, if it were permitted on a Festival, one could make a mistake and come to permit it on Shabbat, since it is drawn after the wick, because it is not obvious to everyone that the reason [it is forbidden on Shabbat is that] since it is a mitzvah upon him to burn it, [the Sages] decreed lest one tilt [the lamp]. Rabbeinu Eliezer raised a difficulty: For here Rabba explains that the reason is a decree regarding a Festival on account of Shabbat, yet below (Shabbat 24b) he derives [that burning consecrated items on a Festival is prohibited] from the verse: "that alone" [Exodus 12:16]! And Rabbeinu Shmuel replied to him: By necessity, below [on 24b] it is Rava, who lived after Abaye, whereas here it is Rabba, as Abaye his student responds to him, and also Rav Chisda, his colleague, disagrees with him. However, it is difficult: Why did Abaye object here, "If so, on a Festival it should be permitted," when he himself derives below [24b] that one may not light with burnt oil from [the verse] "the burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat" [Numbers 28:10]? And it seems [appropriate] to explain: Abaye and Rava below do not hold of what [the Gemara initially] says: "What is the reason that one may not light? Because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival," and they do not accept this decree of [prohibiting impure] terumah on account of consecrated items; rather, they are [merely] explaining: From where do we derive that one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival? And the Rashba explains as follows: "If so, on a Festival it should be permitted" — Granted, if you say that [the mishnah] is dealing with a Festival that fell on Shabbat eve, and the reason is because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival, as Rav Chisda establishes it, that is well; but once you say the reason that one may not light on Shabbat is a decree lest one tilt, now [the Gemara] cannot explain that on a Festival one may not light because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival, for why would a Festival belong to be taught here, since on a Festival it is a different reason? Rather, [according to Rabba], one must explain that on a Festival too [the reason is] lest one tilt — but what [concern of] tilting applies on a Festival? And according to this, the phrasing "If so" is well-settled, which implies that there is a way to explain in another manner such that "on a Festival it should be permitted" would not be difficult, and there is no contradiction of Abaye against Abaye. And if you say: Here Rabba decreed [prohibiting on] a Festival on account of Shabbat, and Shabbat itself is [prohibited lest] one tilt; if so, he holds that we issue a decree to prevent violation of a decree [gezeirah ligezeirah]! Yet at the beginning of our chapter (21a) [the Gemara] says: "That itself is a decree, and shall we arise and issue a decree to prevent violation of a decree?!" And we do not decree [prohibiting a case where] one added oil into molten fat on account of [a case where] one did not add [oil], for even without adding [oil] it is forbidden only on account of that which is not molten. And even though in the case of molten fat we decree a decree to prevent violation of a decree — for we decree [prohibiting molten fat] on account of that which is not molten, and [prohibiting] that which is not molten on account of "lest one tilt" — that is not considered a decree upon a decree, for when it is not molten he will certainly tilt [the lamp], since it is not drawn after the wick; but here, [merely] because it is a mitzvah upon him [to burn it], we cannot say that he will certainly tilt [the lamp]! And the Ri answered: Here it is not considered a decree to prevent violation of a decree, because a Festival and Shabbat are like one another, as we say in the chapter "Bameh Ishah" (below, Shabbat 60a and there) regarding the spiked sandal. And the Rashba finds it difficult: For here we decree [prohibiting on] a Festival on account of Shabbat, whereas at the beginning of [the chapter] "Kol HaKelim" (below, Shabbat 124a and there), we conclude that we do not decree [a Festival on account of Shabbat]! And perhaps one should not compare decrees of the Sages to one another, [specifically] those that are not regarding the same category of labor.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:7:2.hebrew: גזירה יו"ט אטו שבת - וקשה לרשב"א, הא דתנן בפ"ג דביצה (דף כז: ושם): מעשה ושאל ר' טרפון עליה ועל החלה שנטמאת, ואמרו לו: "לא יזיזם ממקומם". והשתא לרבה, אמאי לא יזיזנה? והא חזיא להיסק תחת תבשילו, דלא שייך בה למיגזר יו"ט אטו שבת כמו בשמן! ולפי טעמא ד"אין שורפין קדשים ביום טוב" — ניחא. וצריך לדחוק, דגזרינן חלה בשבת אטו שמן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23b:7:2.english: "[It is] a decree [on] a Festival due to Shabbat" - And the Rashba raises a difficulty from that which we learned in the third chapter of Beitzah (27b and there): An incident occurred where Rabbi Tarfon asked about it [an animal carcass] and about ḥalla that became ritually impure, and they said to him: "One may not move them from their place." And now, according to Rabba, why may he not move it [the ḥalla]? Behold, it is fit for fuel under his cooked food, for it is not applicable regarding it to decree [prohibiting it on] a Festival due to Shabbat, as [is decreed] regarding oil! And according to the reason that "one does not burn sacred items on a Festival," it is well understood; but [according to Rabba] one must force [the answer] that we decree [against] ḥalla on Shabbat on account of oil [and consequently on a Festival on account of Shabbat].
